The Agent had to invent all of this from scratch inside the task loop, which is why 65 iterations were consumed and why edge cases (rounded total vs. inclusive total, DD/MM vs MM/DD, OCR digit confusions) were handled ad-hoc.","related_failures":["OF1","OF2","OF4","OF5"]},{"id":"RC2","summary":"No guidance to prefer the final/rounded total over pre-rounding or pre-tax 'Total' lines","detail":"The task's priority list treats plain 'TOTAL' as a single tier. Real receipts routinely contain multiple 'Total' lines — 'Total (Inclusive of GST)', 'Total incl. of GST', 'Total Rounded', 'Total Amt Rounded', 'Rounding Adj', final 'TOTAL'. Without a rule that says 'when several TOTAL-tier lines exist, prefer the last one that is the rounded/net final total (keywords ROUNDED, NET, GRAND, or the line immediately before CASH/CHANGE)', the extractor cannot reliably pick 23.25 over 23.26 or 102.00 over a misread 702.00.","related_failures":["OF1","OF2"]},{"id":"RC3","summary":"Ambiguous date formats are not disambiguated by receipt locale cues","detail":"Receipts in this dataset are Malaysian and overwhelmingly DD/MM/YYYY. The Agent's DATE_PATTERNS list includes both %d/%m/%Y and %Y/%m/%d but no %m/%d/%Y; however it appears to have accepted a day>12 interpretation that still produced a wrong month for 034.jpg. The Skill gives no rule like 'treat dd/mm/yyyy as the default when the receipt is Malaysian/UK-style, and only fall back to mm/dd/yyyy if the first field is > 12'.","related_failures":["OF4"]},{"id":"RC4","summary":"xlsx Skill does not forbid empty strings for missing fields","detail":"For 078.jpg the Agent wrote total_amount = \"\" instead of a real null. The task spec says 'the value is set to null' on failure, and the grader treats \"\" as different from None. The original xlsx SKILL.md focuses on formulas/formatting and has no 'strict-schema extraction output' section telling the Agent to use Python None (empty cell), avoid NaN strings, write amounts as 2-decimal strings, and sort lexicographically by filename.","related_failures":["OF3"]},{"id":"RC5","summary":"No OCR-robustness rule for digit confusions on the TOTAL line","detail":"'102.00' vs '702.00' and '0' vs '6' confusions are the dominant OCR errors on these scans. The Skill does not tell the Agent to (a) run multiple OCR variants and take the majority value among candidates matching the same keyword, (b) cross-check TOTAL against Subtotal / Payment / Cash-Change arithmetic (total = cash - change) as a tiebreaker, or (c) prefer the TOTAL value that equals the Payment line on the same receipt.","related_failures":["OF1"]},{"id":"RC6","summary":"Agent-loop budget was consumed by per-image debugging","detail":"Iteration accounting shows 65 iterations hit the cap; many were spent re-running OCR with different PSM/preprocess variants on single images. The Skill's existing emphasis on formulas is irrelevant and distracting for this task.","linked_root_causes":["RC4"]},{"skill":"xlsx","defect":"No explicit warning that empty string, 'nan', 'None', and NaN are all distinct from None and will fail line-by-line grading.","linked_root_causes":["RC4"]},{"skill":"openai-vision","defect":"For tasks where a receipt is scanned with heavy OCR noise, there is no cross-reference from image-ocr pointing to vision-based OCR as a fallback for low-confidence Tesseract results. Exclusions must be checked before keyword matching. Keep this generic enough to apply to any priority/exclusion task."},{"target_skill":"image-ocr","change":"Specify a 'pick the final total when multiple TOTAL-tier candidates exist' rule: among candidates in the same tier, prefer the one that (a) appears closest to CASH/PAYMENT/CHANGE lines, (b) contains ROUNDED/NET/GRAND/FINAL, or (c) agrees with the Payment line value. Also add a two-line fallback: if the keyword line has no numeric value, use the last number on the next non-empty line."},{"target_skill":"image-ocr","change":"Document amount normalization: strip currency prefixes (RM, $, €), strip thousand separators, require exactly two decimal places via f\"{value:.2f}\", and return a Python str.
